Find the area between the curve $y=\sqrt{4-x}$, the $y$-axis and the lines $y=0$ and $y=1,$ as shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we make $x$ the subject:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt{4-x} \\ {y}^{2} & =4-x \\ x & =4-{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(4-{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =4\cdot y{|}_{0}^{1}-{\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =4(1-0)-(\frac{1}{3}-0) \\  & =4-\frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{11}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
